newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower as Dec options expire.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower as Dec options expire.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended at the session lows Friday after a late bout of speculative selling, dragging the spot month to within striking distance of key chart support, dealers said.

For much of the day, the expiry of December options set the tone for the outright market, as futures gravitated toward the popular $1,350 strike price. Scattered bargain-hunting by manufacturers also provided an underpinning.
But futures succumbed to speculative liquidation pressure as buying interest fizzled, sinking to session lows at the closing bell.
December futures fell $8 a tonne on the day, to $1,345, down from a high of $1,355. Second-position March also fell $8, to $1,384, while the outer months eased between $9 and $11.

Today's close brought the market to the lower end of its recent range, as December looked poised to test key support at $1,341. If that level were breached, chartists said the market would next take aim at its recent low of $1,329.
To the upside, December would need to clear $1,378-1,382, while resistance basis March was assessed at a chart gap between $1,404 and $1,408.
The day's volume was fairly steady, at 8,140 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
